item.title: One Pair Across Every Shot

turns.text: Make a realistic, silent 15-second widescreen story in three shots: a woman with a freckled face and red pixie cut drops a red scarf; a man with a shaved head and round glasses picks it up; he returns it and they smile. Both adults, on a quiet street. Show both faces clearly in every shot and keep exactly the same two faces throughout—no changing actors between cuts.

must_haves: One assembled 15-second 16:9 film tells the story in three distinct shots.
The woman retains the same facial structure, freckles and red pixie cut in all three shots.
The man retains the same facial structure, shaved head and round glasses in all three shots; the two identities never merge or swap.
Both faces are clearly visible in every shot, not hidden by rear views, distant framing or object-only cutaways.
The red scarf is dropped by the woman, picked up by the man and returned to her in that order, ending with mutual smiles.
The film looks realistic and has no audible soundtrack.

args.name: The Red Scarf — Three-Shot Street Story

style.prompt: Realistic live-action short film, exactly 15 seconds, widescreen 16:9, silent, three consecutive shots of five seconds each. A simple warm human encounter on a quiet pedestrian street in soft natural daylight. EXACTLY TWO ADULT ACTORS throughout: woman age 30 with a clearly freckled face, short copper-red pixie haircut, green eyes, cream coat; man age 35 with completely shaved head, round thin dark-framed glasses, brown eyes, navy jacket. Lock both identities: same facial structure, freckles, hair, glasses, outfits and proportions across every cut. No actor substitutions, face morphing, extra people, background pedestrians, text or subtitles. Both faces must be clearly visible and recognizable IN EVERY SHOT, including while picking up the scarf: use frontal or three-quarter two-shots, never backs, profiles, cropped faces, object closeups or obstructed faces. Shot 1, 0–5s: medium-wide frontal two-shot, woman on frame left and man on frame right, both faces sharp. Woman accidentally releases a single bright red scarf from her hand; it falls to pavement between them. They notice it. Shot 2, 5–10s: cut to a slightly lower, wider frontal two-shot retaining exactly the same two faces. Woman remains upright at left, visible face looking slightly toward camera and man. Man at right bends at knees into a squat with head held up so his entire face and round glasses remain visible, reaches down, picks up that same red scarf, then rises. Keep BOTH faces in frame and sharply readable throughout the full movement. Shot 3, 10–15s: cut to a medium frontal two-shot of the identical woman at left and identical man at right. He offers her the red scarf, she takes it, they exchange warm natural smiles with their faces angled three-quarter toward the camera so both remain clearly visible. Believable hands and fabric motion, restrained acting, consistent geography and lighting, natural skin texture, realistic proportions, moderate depth of field keeping both faces sharp, no music, no dialogue, no sound.
